title: Acute Dyspnea — POCUS & NIV
keywords: A-lines lung sliding COPD asthma PE
absent lung sliding pneumothorax lung point
sources: Critical Vector — EM Pocket Guide: Acute Dyspnea / NIV (BLUE Protocol; ATS 2024)

changelog.change: Initial entry — POCUS pattern → diagnosis → first move table, NIV/HFNC start settings, COPD bundle, and the NIV-failure / early-intubation pearls.

summary: Lung POCUS at the bedside, done alongside O2 and IV access, sorts undifferentiated dyspnea faster than a chest X-ray (~94% sensitive for cardiogenic oedema). NIV failure that then needs emergent RSI carries higher mortality than an elective early intubation — reassess at 1 hour and do not 'NIV and wait'.

rows: BiPAP (IPAP 10–15 / EPAP 5–8) + furosemide 40–80 mg IV; echo for LVEF; BNP/NT-proBNP
COPD: bronchodilators + BiPAP · Asthma: SABA nebs + Mg 2 g IV · PE: Wells/PERC → CTPA
Lung point confirms (100% specific); needle decompression if unstable, then chest tube
Antibiotics; low intubation threshold if bilateral; worsening hypoxia on HFNC → prepare for RSI
Anticoagulate; if haemodynamic compromise → systemic thrombolysis (alteplase 100 mg/2 h, or 0.6 mg/kg over 15 min in arrest)
Diagnostic thoracentesis if > 10 mm; apply Light's criteria
10–15 cmH2O (net pressure support = IPAP − EPAP, target 8–12)

items: Flow: start 40–60 L/min, titrate to comfort and SpO2.
FiO2: start 0.6–0.8; wean below 0.5 within 1–2 h if improving.
ROX index = (SpO2/FiO2) / RR — < 4.88 at 12 h predicts a high HFNC failure risk; prepare for intubation.
Surviving Sepsis 2026: HFNC preferred over conventional O2 AND over NIV for acute hypoxaemic respiratory failure (conditional).
Bronchodilators: salbutamol 2.5 mg + ipratropium 0.5 mg neb q20 min ×3.
BiPAP: IPAP 10–15 / EPAP 4–8; reduces intubation by ~50% and reduces mortality — first-line over intubation if the patient is cooperative.
Corticosteroids: methylprednisolone 125 mg IV once, then prednisone 40 mg PO ×5 days (REDUCE trial — non-inferior to 14 days).
Magnesium sulfate 2 g IV over 20 min (adjunct; stronger evidence in asthma).
Antibiotics if ≥ 2 Anthonisen criteria (↑ dyspnoea + ↑ sputum volume + ↑ purulence).
Heliox 70:30 as an adjunct in severe refractory bronchospasm.

body.text: NIV failure signs — worsening RR, SpO2, or mentation after 1 h; spontaneous tidal volume > 9 mL/kg IBW (P-SILI risk); inability to protect the airway; haemodynamic deterioration → intubate early, not late. In a COPD patient: pH < 7.30 and not improving at 1 h = intubate. Consider CO poisoning (SpO2 falsely normal), and tension pneumothorax in a ventilated patient with sudden desaturation + collapse (decompress before the CXR).
